_: A director profile: the film language a storyboard is written in (by an agent or an LLM), and the engine defaults. defaults — shot fields by default (a shot overrides them); min_shot — a shot shorter than this breaks the language (a warning in make timeline).

language.editing: Long takes of 20–90 s, 25–40 shots per film. Simple cuts; the transition is often made by the camera itself (cam → cam_to): from the room to the window, from a face to an object. No dissolves. Several cues in a row inside one shot.
language.camera: Tripod and rails: no shake (hand 0). A slow lateral track (drift 6–15 cm per shot), a very slow push-in (push 4–12 cm over 30–60 s), a long gaze at an object. The camera slightly below eye level, symmetry, deep staging: foreground — an object, middle — a person, distance — a window/garden/fog.
language.people: People are almost still: from behind, in profile, by the window, deep in the frame; an occasional look into the camera. Movement — a slow walk across the frame. Close-ups of faces — long and static.
language.light_color: Natural light: a window, an overcast day, rain; the lamp is a living flame. Muted film stock (green-brown). The doctor's inner world and the void — monochrome or sepia (grade in the light preset).
language.elements: Water (drops, puddles, rain outside the window), wind (grass, a curtain), fire (a lamp, a candle), fog (fog in the preset), down and dust in a beam, a mirror/reflection, levitation (a slow rise in the void).
language.time: Silence: after important paragraphs — pauses of 4–12 s (holds), the shot lasts, the voice is silent; natural sounds go on.
language.sound: Drops, rain, wind, a distant train, a clock; music rarely — an organ chorale or a low electronic hum (drone).
